## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Security — Web & API

Assesses the browser-facing and transport security of HTTP applications and APIs: CSP, security response headers,
HSTS and HTTPS/TLS enforcement, CORS, API response headers, HTTP method and content-type handling, and credentials in
URLs, using local, pinned summaries of OWASP and vendor guidance.

#### Inputs

HTTP pipeline and middleware setup, security/header configuration (framework config classes, `settings*.py`),
CORS configuration, web-server and proxy configuration (`web.config`, `nginx*.conf`, `.htaccess`), HTTP listener
configuration (`launchSettings.json`, `application*.properties|yml`, `Dockerfile`), REST controllers and file-download
endpoints, and HTML layout templates, per `compliance-inventory`.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/owasp-web-api.md` — CSP-01…11, HDR-01…19, RST-01…12, H5-01…05, HST-01…02, TLS-01…05,
  A02-01…05. Always load.
- `references/standards/dotnet-web-api.md` — DNW-01…10. Load when language `csharp` is detected.
- `references/standards/java-web-api.md` — JVW-01…11. Load when language `java` is detected.
- `references/standards/python-web-api.md` — PYW-01…09. Load when language `python` is detected.
- `references/standards/mdn-web-api.md` — MDN-01 (CSP Trusted Types). Always load.
- `references/standards/node-web-api.md` — NDW-01…05. Load when language `javascript` is detected.
- Framework elements apply only when that framework (and, for Django, the named middleware) is in use.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill, and never use remembered defaults: a header, HTTPS or CORS default counts
  only when a localized element states it. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md`, the standards files that apply (above), and
   `references/languages/<id>.md` for each detected language (detection signals only; they cite no standard).
2. Classify the target from its files: HTML-serving (views, templates, static HTML or SPA host served by the app),
   API-only (endpoints returning JSON/XML, no HTML), or neither (subject N/A). For API-only targets mark SEC-WA-01,
   -04 and -11 N/A ("API-only: browser-rendering headers not applicable").
3. Find where response headers are set: application code and configuration, framework defaults stated by a
   localized (Default) element, and web-server/proxy/IaC files in the subject's list. A header set in any of them
   counts as set. A header missing everywhere fails at confidence `medium` for ASP.NET Core, Spring Security,
   Django and Express (helmet defaults, NDW-01); for other frameworks judge explicit values only and add
   `localized-standard-gap: <framework> default for <header> not localized` to `notes`.
4. For each check SEC-WA-01…SEC-WA-11, evaluate the elements it lists against the subject's files, using the
   signal files to find evidence and the evidence notes in `checklist.md`. No CORS configuration at all passes
   SEC-WA-05. An HTTPS-only API without HSTS passes SEC-WA-02. Don't fail on speculation. Use confidence `medium`
   unless the evidence is unambiguous.
5. Ownership: don't report error-response bodies or diagnostic endpoints (operational), cookie flags, CSRF,
   session IDs in URLs, JWT/API-key handling, method or management-endpoint authorization (identity-access), XSS
   encoding, request size limits or XXE (input-injection), method semantics, idempotency, status codes or error
   format (api-design), rate limits (reliability), caching of public assets (performance), or library versions
   (dependency-management), or personal data (not credentials) in URLs, client storage or API responses
   (review-data-protection DPR-02/DPR-03). CSP is defense in depth; never report a missing CSP as an XSS vulnerability.
6. Severity: MUST/REVIEW elements take the check's default from `checklist.md`; SHOULD elements one level lower
   (Error → Warning, Warning → Information); HDR-11 is advisory and never fails on its own. When several elements
   fail on the same evidence, write one finding at the highest severity. `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is the
   check's default.
7. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `HDR-01`); the report script derives `standard` and `url`
   from it, so don't write them. Prefer a vendor element, then a cheat-sheet element, then an A02 element (cite A02
   only when nothing more specific fits). For an element marked (Default), cite the OWASP element it supports and name
   the vendor element in the recommendation. Where vendor guidance is weaker than an OWASP element, the OWASP element
   decides.
8. If the reference date (date part of `startedAt`) is more than 9 months after a standards file's "Localized"
   date, add `localized-standard-stale: <file> localized <date>` to `notes`.

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

## File: `references/checklist.md`

### Checklist — Security: Web & API

Subject: Security

Each check is evaluated through the elements it lists; every element belongs to exactly one check. Element
definitions, anchors and citation bases are in `standards/`. Severity rules (SHOULD elements one level lower; HDR-11
advisory) are in `../SKILL.md`. **Applies to:** `HTML` = HTML-serving targets only; `API` = targets with API endpoints
or file downloads; `all` = every target with HTTP endpoints (`../SKILL.md` step 2).

| id | Sub-subject | Check | Default severity | Applies to | Elements | Source |
|----|-------------|-------|------------------|------------|----------|--------|
| SEC-WA-01 | Web & API | HTML responses carry an enforced Content-Security-Policy header, preferably strict (nonces/hashes), with no `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval` for scripts | Warning | HTML | CSP-01, CSP-03 … CSP-09, JVW-06, PYW-06, MDN-01, NDW-04 | CSP, JVW, PYW, MDN, NDW |
| SEC-WA-02 | Web & API | `Strict-Transport-Security` is sent on HTTPS responses with a long `max-age` and `includeSubDomains` | Warning | HTML, API serving HTTP | HDR-07, HST-01, HST-02, DNW-03, DNW-04, JVW-03, PYW-02 | HDR, HST, DNW, JVW, PYW |
| SEC-WA-03 | Web & API | `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` is sent on all responses | Warning | all | HDR-03, JVW-01, PYW-01 | HDR, JVW, PYW |
| SEC-WA-04 | Web & API | Pages can't be framed by untrusted sites (`frame-ancestors`, with `X-Frame-Options` for older browsers) | Warning | HTML | HDR-01, CSP-11, JVW-02, PYW-05 | HDR, CSP, JVW, PYW |
| SEC-WA-05 | Web & API | CORS is off unless needed, scoped to specific trusted origins on the endpoints that need it, never any-origin or reflected origin with credentials, and never used as access control | Error | all | HDR-09, RST-10, H5-01, H5-02, H5-03, DNW-05, DNW-06, DNW-07, JVW-09, JVW-10, JVW-11, PYW-09, A02-04 | HDR, RST, H5, DNW, JVW, PYW, A02 |
| SEC-WA-06 | Web & API | All endpoints use HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ and strong ciphers; HTML sites redirect HTTP to HTTPS, APIs refuse HTTP; no mixed content | Error | all | RST-01, TLS-01 … TLS-05, CSP-10, H5-04, DNW-01, DNW-02, JVW-08, PYW-03, PYW-04, A02-05, NDW-03 | RST, TLS, CSP, H5, DNW, JVW, PYW, A02, NDW |
| SEC-WA-07 | Web & API | Response headers don't reveal server or framework versions (`Server`, `X-Powered-By`, `X-AspNet-Version`, `X-AspNetMvc-Version`) | Warning | all | HDR-14 … HDR-17, NDW-02 | HDR, NDW |
| SEC-WA-08 | Web & API | API responses and file downloads carry safe headers: correct `Content-Type`, `no-store` on sensitive responses, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, attachment download headers, and no sensitive data in Cache API storage | Warning | API | HDR-05, HDR-06, HDR-19, RST-06 … RST-09, H5-05, DNW-09, JVW-04, NDW-05 | HDR, RST, H5, DNW, JVW, NDW |
| SEC-WA-09 | Web & API | Endpoints accept only allowlisted HTTP methods and declared content types (405/415), never copy `Accept` into `Content-Type`, and expose no unnecessary methods or formats | Warning | API | RST-02 … RST-05, DNW-08, DNW-10, A02-03 | RST, DNW, A02 |
| SEC-WA-10 | Web & API | Passwords, tokens and API keys aren't sent in URLs; sensitive request data travels in headers or bodies | Warning | API | RST-11, RST-12 | RST |
| SEC-WA-11 | Web & API | HTML responses set browser policy headers (Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP, CORP) and send no obsolete or harmful headers (`X-XSS-Protection: 1`, `Expect-CT`, HPKP, `X-Content-Security-Policy`) | Warning | HTML | CSP-02, HDR-02, HDR-04, HDR-08, HDR-10 … HDR-13, HDR-18, JVW-05, JVW-07, PYW-07, PYW-08, A02-01, A02-02, NDW-01 | CSP, HDR, JVW, PYW, A02, NDW |

Totals: 54 OWASP cheat-sheet + 5 Top 10 + 10 DNW + 11 JVW + 9 PYW = 89 elements across 11 checks.

Applicability: an HTML-serving target is judged on all 11 checks (SEC-WA-08 … -10 only if it also has API endpoints or
file downloads). For an API-only target, mark SEC-WA-01, -04 and -11 N/A with the reason "API-only: browser-rendering
headers not applicable (hdr#content-security-policy-csp, rst#security-headers)". A target with no HTTP endpoints in
its files makes the subject N/A.

#### Evidence notes

- **Header set or missing.** A response header counts as set when application code or configuration sets it, a
  localized (Default) element says the framework sends it and the files don't disable it, or a web-server, proxy or
  IaC file in the subject's list sets it (nginx `add_header` / Apache `Header set` without `always` count, but the
  recommendation notes the header is missing on error responses). If none holds: for ASP.NET Core, Spring Security
  and Django fail the element at confidence `medium`, with the recommendation "if a reverse proxy or CDN outside the
  repository adds this header, record that in the repository"; for any other framework judge explicit insecure values
  only, and add `localized-standard-gap: <framework> default for <header> not localized` to `notes`.
- **SEC-WA-01:** fail when an HTML-serving target has no enforced CSP (CSP-01), or when the policy allows
  `'unsafe-inline'`/`'unsafe-eval'` for scripts (CSP-05). CSP is defense in depth: never report a missing CSP as an
  XSS vulnerability (`review-security-input-injection` owns XSS).
- **SEC-WA-02:** `max-age` below `31536000` fails HST-01 (SHOULD); the recommendation names `63072000`. A missing
  `includeSubDomains` fails HST-02 (SHOULD). `preload` without evidence of an intended preload submission goes in the
  recommendation only. An API-only target that serves HTTPS only passes without the header (DNW-04); it fails only if
  the API also serves HTTP.
- **SEC-WA-05:** fail on wildcard or reflected origins on non-public endpoints, any-origin with credentials,
  `Origin`-based authorization, and bare `@CrossOrigin`/global mappings without `allowedOrigins`. Origins read from
  configuration pass unless the configured value is `*` or empty-means-all. No CORS configuration at all is a pass
  (HDR-09: the Same Origin Policy applies).
- **SEC-WA-06:** fail on HTTP listeners in production configuration (launch profiles under Development don't count),
  API endpoints whose only HTTP protection is a redirect (TLS-04, DNW-01), explicit TLS 1.0/1.1/SSL or weak cipher
  settings, and `http://` subresources in HTML templates. Server-side TLS settings outside the repository aren't
  judged. ASP.NET Core's default 307 redirect is not a failure.
- **SEC-WA-07:** fail on code or config that **adds** or explicitly keeps version-revealing headers (`X-Powered-By`,
  `X-AspNet-Version`, `X-AspNetMvc-Version`, informative `Server`), and on .NET Framework `web.config`/`Global.asax`
  missing the HDR-16/HDR-17 settings. The Kestrel `Server` default is not localized: ASP.NET Core fails only on
  explicit evidence. Error-body content is not judged here (`review-security-operational` SEC-OP-01).
- **SEC-WA-08:** judge only API responses and file downloads. `Cache-Control` for responses carrying session IDs or
  authentication data belongs to `review-security-identity-access`; here it covers all other sensitive API responses
  (HDR-06) and the general API recommendation (RST-07).
- **SEC-WA-09:** fail on explicit any-method handlers or TRACE enabled (RST-02), bodies parsed without a content-type
  check (RST-03), `Accept` copied into `Content-Type` (RST-05), and XML formatters enabled on JSON-only APIs (RST-04).
  Framework method-mapping defaults aren't localized, so only explicit code counts.
- **SEC-WA-10:** fail when routes, model binding or client calls in the files put passwords, tokens or API keys in a
  URL path or query string (`?api_key=`, `[FromQuery] string apiKey`, `request.GET["token"]`,
  `@RequestParam("password")`). Session IDs in URLs and OAuth implicit-grant tokens belong to identity-access.
- **SEC-WA-11:** HTML-serving targets only. Harmful values (`X-XSS-Protection: 1…`, `Expect-CT`, HPKP, obsolete CSP
  header names, `Referrer-Policy: unsafe-url`) fail at MUST level. A missing Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP
  or CORP is a SHOULD failure (Information). HDR-11 (COEP) is advisory only.

## File: `references/standards/owasp-web-api.md`

*Load rule: CSP-01…11, HDR-01…19, RST-01…12, H5-01…05, HST-01…02, TLS-01…05, A02-01…05. Always load.*

### OWASP web and API security guidance — localized summary

- Level: `MUST` where the source says must/must not/never/do not/ensure, gives an unqualified imperative ("Remove…",
  "Use…", "Discard…"), or names a prohibited practice. `SHOULD` for recommendations (should/recommended/prefer/
  consider). Top 10 elements use `REVIEW` for "Description" weaknesses and mapped CWEs (`REVIEW` is treated like
  `MUST`). HDR-11 is **Advisory**: cited in recommendations only, never fails on its own. Severity rules are in
  `../../SKILL.md`.
- Applicability (`../../SKILL.md` step 2): HTML-serving targets are judged on every check; API-only targets skip
  SEC-WA-01, -04 and -11 (browser-rendering headers; hdr#content-security-policy-csp, rst#security-headers) and get the
  API forms of those protections through SEC-WA-08.
- Language-agnostic files (`web.config`, `nginx*.conf`, `.htaccess`, `httpd.conf`, HAProxy, `Caddyfile`, IaC) have no
  language id. Evaluate them with the elements below whenever they are in the subject's file list. Signals:
  - nginx `add_header` / Apache `Header set` without `always` count as setting the header, but the recommendation notes
    that it is missing on error responses (hdr#nginx, hdr#apache); IIS `<customHeaders>` under `<httpProtocol>`;
  - nginx `server_tokens on`, Apache `ServerTokens Full`/`ServerSignature On` (HDR-14);
  - `ssl_protocols`/`SSLProtocol` including `TLSv1`/`TLSv1.1`/`SSLv3` (TLS-01); `ssl_ciphers`/`SSLCipherSuite` with
    `NULL`, `aNULL`, `EXPORT` or `RSA` key-transport suites (TLS-02);
  - `listen 80` without `return 301 https://…` on an HTML site (TLS-03); a port-80 server block proxying an API (TLS-04);
  - `http://` `<script src>`/`<link href>` in HTML templates (TLS-05);
  - `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` containing `frame-ancestors` (CSP-11).

The Headers sheet repeats "Recommendation" headings; their anchors are `recommendation`, `recommendation_1` …
`recommendation_21`, in page order.

#### Content Security Policy Cheat Sheet (CSP)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CSP-01 | MUST | Deliver an enforced policy in the `Content-Security-Policy` header on every HTML response, not just the index page. Report-Only alone doesn't enforce ("fail open"). A `<meta>` policy is a fallback only when headers can't be set; it can't carry `frame-ancestors`, `sandbox` or reporting. | no CSP in middleware/server config; Report-Only only; CSP on one route | SEC-WA-01 |
| CSP-02 | MUST | Don't send the obsolete `X-Content-Security-Policy` or `X-WebKit-CSP` headers. | those header names in code/config | SEC-WA-11 |
| CSP-03 | SHOULD | Prefer a strict CSP: nonce- or hash-based `script-src` (optionally `'strict-dynamic'`) with `object-src 'none'` and `base-uri 'none'`. | allowlist-only `script-src` listing many hosts | SEC-WA-01 |
| CSP-04 | MUST | Nonces are unique random values generated per response and rendered by the templating engine. Never use middleware that adds nonces to every `<script>` tag, and never use a fixed nonce. | constant nonce string; HTML rewriting that inserts `nonce=` | SEC-WA-01 |
| CSP-05 | MUST | Script sources (`script-src`, or `default-src` as the fallback) don't allow `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'`. Move inline code and inline event handlers to files and `addEventListener`. | `script-src 'unsafe-inline'`/`'unsafe-eval'` | SEC-WA-01 |
| CSP-06 | SHOULD | Style sources avoid `'unsafe-inline'` too. | `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` | SEC-WA-01 |
| CSP-07 | SHOULD | A non-strict policy limits `default-src` to `'self'` (or `'none'` plus explicit directives) and sets `form-action`. Don't loosen it with broad sources; overly permissive policies lead to bypasses. | `default-src *`; `script-src https:`/`*`; no `form-action` | SEC-WA-01 |
| CSP-08 | SHOULD | Set `object-src 'none'` when plugins aren't needed. Don't rely on the removed `plugin-types` or `prefetch-src` directives. | `plugin-types`/`prefetch-src` used as controls; no `object-src` and no restrictive `default-src` | SEC-WA-01 |
| CSP-09 | SHOULD | Report violations with `report-to` (an endpoint from `Reporting-Endpoints`), with `report-uri` kept only as a fallback. A Report-Only policy may run alongside the enforced one to test changes. | only the deprecated `report-uri` | SEC-WA-01 |
| CSP-10 | SHOULD | Use `upgrade-insecure-requests` while migrating a site from HTTP to HTTPS. | HTTPS site with legacy `http://` asset URLs and no directive | SEC-WA-06 |
| CSP-11 | MUST | Restrict framing with `frame-ancestors` in a header (`'none'`, `'self'` or named trusted origins). The directive is ignored in `<meta>` and doesn't fall back to `default-src`. | `frame-ancestors *`; `frame-ancestors` only in a meta tag | SEC-WA-04 |

#### HTTP Security Response Headers Cheat Sheet (HDR)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HDR-01 | MUST | Pages with interactive content can't be framed by other sites. Prefer CSP `frame-ancestors`; also send `X-Frame-Options: DENY`. Redirects and JSON responses gain nothing from `X-Frame-Options`. | no frame protection on HTML responses | SEC-WA-04 |
| HDR-02 | MUST | Don't enable the browser XSS filter: omit `X-XSS-Protection` or send `X-XSS-Protection: 0`. It can create XSS in otherwise safe sites. | `X-XSS-Protection: 1` / `1; mode=block` | SEC-WA-11 |
| HDR-03 | MUST | Send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and set `Content-Type` correctly throughout the site. | no nosniff in middleware, framework or server config | SEC-WA-03 |
| HDR-04 | SHOULD | Set `Referrer-Policy` explicitly (`strict-origin-when-cross-origin` or stricter) instead of relying on browser defaults. | no Referrer-Policy; `unsafe-url`; `no-referrer-when-downgrade` | SEC-WA-11 |
| HDR-05 | SHOULD | Responses declare the correct `Content-Type`; HTML responses include `charset`. This matters most when the client renders untrusted content. | `text/html` without charset; user content served without an explicit type | SEC-WA-08 |
| HDR-06 | MUST | Sensitive responses send `Cache-Control: no-store`. `private` only keeps them out of shared caches, and `no-cache` doesn't prevent storage. Don't rely on default caching, and keep sensitive responses out of application-managed caches. | sensitive endpoints without no-store; `no-cache` used as the protection | SEC-WA-08 |
| HDR-07 | MUST | Send `Strict-Transport-Security` on HTTPS responses. The recommended value is `max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`; add `preload` only when deliberately submitting to the preload list. | no HSTS in code, framework or server config | SEC-WA-02 |
| HDR-08 | MUST | Don't send `Expect-CT`; remove it from existing code. | `Expect-CT` header set | SEC-WA-11 |
| HDR-09 | MUST | If `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is used, set specific origins instead of `*`. `*` is acceptable only for public resources meant for any origin. No CORS header means the Same Origin Policy applies. | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on non-public endpoints | SEC-WA-05 |
| HDR-10 | SHOULD | HTML documents send `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`. It isn't meaningful for non-browser API clients. | no COOP on HTML responses; `unsafe-none` | SEC-WA-11 |
| HDR-11 | SHOULD | `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` where cross-origin resources are prepared for it. **Advisory only; never fails on its own**, because the source warns that it blocks resources that aren't configured for it. | — (recommendation text) | SEC-WA-11 |
| HDR-12 | SHOULD | Send `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-site` to limit which origins can include a resource. | no CORP; `cross-origin` on private resources | SEC-WA-11 |
| HDR-13 | SHOULD | Send `Permissions-Policy` that disables browser features the site doesn't use, or allows them only to authorized origins. | no Permissions-Policy; `*` allowlists | SEC-WA-11 |
| HDR-14 | MUST | Remove the `Server` header or set a non-informative value. | informative `Server` value set; nginx `server_tokens on` | SEC-WA-07 |
| HDR-15 | MUST | Remove all `X-Powered-By` headers. | `X-Powered-By` added in code or config | SEC-WA-07 |
| HDR-16 | MUST | ASP.NET (.NET Framework): disable `X-AspNet-Version` with `<httpRuntime enableVersionHeader="false" />`. | `web.config` `<system.web>` without it | SEC-WA-07 |
| HDR-17 | MUST | ASP.NET MVC (.NET Framework): disable `X-AspNetMvc-Version` with `MvcHandler.DisableMvcResponseHeader = true`. | `Global.asax` without it | SEC-WA-07 |
| HDR-18 | MUST | Don't send `Public-Key-Pins` or `Public-Key-Pins-Report-Only`. | HPKP headers; Spring `httpPublicKeyPinning(…)` | SEC-WA-11 |
| HDR-19 | SHOULD | Serve user-provided files with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` for unknown or binary types, and `nosniff`. | download endpoints returning uploads inline with a stored or client-supplied type | SEC-WA-08 |

#### REST Security Cheat Sheet (RST)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RST-01 | MUST | REST services expose only HTTPS endpoints. | `http://` listener URLs for API hosts | SEC-WA-06 |
| RST-02 | MUST | Allowlist the HTTP methods each endpoint accepts and reject others with `405`. | handlers explicitly accepting every method; `TRACE` enabled | SEC-WA-09 |
| RST-03 | MUST | For requests with a body, require a supported `Content-Type` and reject others with `415`. Don't require one on requests without a body. | raw body parsed as JSON/XML without checking the declared type | SEC-WA-09 |
| RST-04 | SHOULD | Declare and document the content types each endpoint consumes and produces (e.g. `@Consumes`/`@Produces`), so that unintended types such as XML (an XXE vector) aren't accepted. | XML formatters enabled on a JSON-only API; no declared types | SEC-WA-09 |
| RST-05 | MUST | Never copy the `Accept` header into the response `Content-Type`. Pick a supported type that matches `Accept`; return `406` only when nothing matches and no default is supplied. | `Content-Type` set from `Accept` | SEC-WA-09 |
| RST-06 | MUST | The response `Content-Type` matches the body (e.g. `application/json`, not `application/javascript` or `text/html` for JSON). Services that return script code take extra care against header injection. | JSON written as `text/html` or `text/plain` | SEC-WA-08 |
| RST-07 | SHOULD | API responses that browsers may consume send `Cache-Control: no-store`. | API pipeline with no cache directive | SEC-WA-08 |
| RST-08 | SHOULD | API responses that browsers may consume send `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Frame-Options: DENY` for older browsers. | no framing protection on API responses | SEC-WA-08 |
| RST-09 | SHOULD | APIs that return, or may return, HTML also send `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'`, a restrictive `Permissions-Policy` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. Fails only when the files show the API returning HTML. | HTML-producing API responses without these headers | SEC-WA-08 |
| RST-10 | SHOULD | Disable CORS headers when cross-domain calls aren't expected; otherwise be as specific as possible. | global any-origin policy | SEC-WA-05 |
| RST-11 | MUST | Passwords, security tokens and API keys never appear in URLs, because URLs are captured in server logs. | `?apiKey=`, `?token=`, `?password=` in routes, bindings, client calls | SEC-WA-10 |
| RST-12 | SHOULD | Send sensitive data in the body or headers for `POST`/`PUT`, and in an HTTP header for `GET`. | sensitive filters passed as GET query parameters | SEC-WA-10 |

#### HTML5 Security Cheat Sheet — CORS and offline sections (H5)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H5-01 | MUST | Allow only selected, trusted origins in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Don't use `*`, and never return the request's `Origin` without checking it against an allowlist. | origin echoed from the request; allow-all origin predicates | SEC-WA-05 |
| H5-02 | MUST | Responses with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` carry no sensitive content. Set CORS headers only on URLs that need cross-domain access, not across the whole domain. | global wildcard policy covering authenticated endpoints | SEC-WA-05 |
| H5-03 | MUST | CORS isn't access control: ordinary `GET`/`POST` requests still perform access control, and the `Origin` header alone never decides access. | authorization decided by the `Origin` value | SEC-WA-05 |
| H5-04 | MUST | Discard requests received over plain HTTP that carry HTTPS origins (mixed content). | — | SEC-WA-06 |
| H5-05 | MUST | Service workers don't put sensitive responses into the Cache API, which ignores HTTP caching headers. They explicitly exclude and delete them, are registered only from the app's own origin over HTTPS, and have a restricted scope. | `cache.put`/`addAll` of authenticated API responses; broad worker scope | SEC-WA-08 |

#### HTTP Strict Transport Security Cheat Sheet (HST)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HST-01 | SHOULD | Use a long `max-age` once HTTPS is stable; the recommended header uses two years (`63072000`). Short values (e.g. one day) are for initial rollout only. Fails below `31536000` (one year). | `max-age` below `31536000` in production config | SEC-WA-02 |
| HST-02 | SHOULD | Add `includeSubDomains` when all subdomains use HTTPS. Without it, cookie attacks through subdomains stay possible. | HSTS without `includeSubDomains` | SEC-WA-02 |

#### Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet — protocols, ciphers, application (TLS)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TLS-01 | MUST | Default to TLS 1.3 and allow TLS 1.2 only for compatibility. TLS 1.0/1.1 and SSLv2/v3 are disabled. | `SslProtocols.Tls`/`Tls11`; `server.ssl.enabled-protocols` with `TLSv1`/`TLSv1.1`; Python `ssl` minimum below TLS 1.2 | SEC-WA-06 |
| TLS-02 | MUST | Disable null, anonymous, EXPORT, RSA key-transport and static-DH cipher suites. Prefer AEAD suites (with ECDHE for TLS 1.2). | explicit cipher lists containing `NULL`, `anon`, `EXPORT`, `TLS_RSA_*` | SEC-WA-06 |
| TLS-03 | SHOULD | Use TLS for all pages, not just sensitive ones. A public HTTP listener only redirects to HTTPS, backed by HSTS. | HTTP routes served without a redirect | SEC-WA-06 |
| TLS-04 | SHOULD | API-only endpoints don't serve HTTP at all; where that isn't possible, they fail HTTP requests instead of redirecting. | an HTTPS redirect as an API's only HTTP protection | SEC-WA-06 |
| TLS-05 | SHOULD | HTTPS pages don't load scripts, styles or other resources over plain HTTP. | `http://` `<script src>`/`<link href>` in templates | SEC-WA-06 |

## File: `references/standards/mdn-web-api.md`

*Load rule: MDN-01 (CSP Trusted Types). Always load.*

### MDN Web Docs — browser security directives — localized summary

- Level: `SHOULD` (MDN documents the directive and gives no normative level; it is defense in depth). A failed `SHOULD`
  element scores one level below the check's default (`../../SKILL.md` step 6). Never report its absence as an XSS
  vulnerability: XSS encoding and DOM sinks are judged by `review-security-input-injection` SEC-II-08.

#### SEC-WA-01 — Content Security Policy

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MDN-01 | SHOULD | HTML apps whose own scripts write to DOM XSS sinks set `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` in their CSP (with a `trusted-types` policy allowlist), so sinks accept only values created by Trusted Type policies, not strings. | CSP set, but the app's scripts use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML` or `document.write` and the CSP has no `require-trusted-types-for` | SEC-WA-01 |
